The record:
Write the overview of the executive synopsis for the incident on io-shop below: a short paragraph in plain words, for the people who lead the company rather than the engineers who responded - what happened, how long it lasted, what it cost the business and the people who responded, and how it was resolved.

What a reader saw: Shoppers' account pages failed
Why, in plain words: The outside company that handles the shop's payments began refusing the shop's requests to look up shoppers' saved cards, and each time that happened the shop's account page failed along with the lookup.

Figures:
- How long it lasted: at least 7m 21s {duration}
- Requests failing at the worst minute: 100.0% {peak_error_rate}
- What it cost the shop in takings (estimated by Argus): at least 15,583.55 USD {customer_loss}
- Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.

What was done to end it:
- Argus: refused to act on a suspected cause - the failure is in a service another company runs, and nothing Argus can do reaches it - ask IO Payments Ltd to restore io-pay, and no code fix is looked for - not taken

Name {duration} and {customer_loss} in your overview.
Write no figure yourself - not in digits, not spelled out, and not as a word that sizes it ("a brief outage", "a minor loss", "tripled"). Where a figure goes, write its name, braces and all, and the synopsis writes the figure in.
Say nothing about how the incident was resolved beyond what the list of what was done says: a draft fix has not run, and nothing it would do has happened.
Speak of Argus by name, never as "we", "our" or "us": Argus is the system that responded, and each line of what was done says who did it.
Where you say who was affected, say which ones, as the cause does, or that some were, where it does not say which - never how many, and never all of them, where the cause does not say all.
Keep "likely" on what the cause says is likely, and only there.

Call submit_executive_overview with your overview.

The postmortem it is written from:
Shoppers' account pages failed
Incident: HighErrorRate on io-shop
Date: Nov 12, 2026, 17:17 UTC, not back to normal by 17:24:21 UTC
Status: Draft. 0 of 3 action items are done.
Written by: Argus Postmortem agent, Nov 12, 2026, 17:27:13 UTC. Not reviewed yet. Each part is as of when the work it reports ended, which the timeline dates; who ended the incident is as of now.
First told: Argus posted in Slack, Nov 12, 2026, 17:23:35 UTC
Ended by: Argus: escalated to a person, Nov 12, 2026, 17:24:21 UTC - no code fix looked for

Summary
The service broke at 17:17 UTC and was not back to normal by 17:24:21 UTC, at least 7 minutes 21 seconds later. 97.9% of requests failed while it was broken, against 1.1% before it began. At its worst, 100.0% failed. So far, the shop's takings fell short of the same hours on earlier weeks by at least 15,583.55 USD, beyond how much those hours vary on their own. The outside company that handles the shop's payments began refusing the shop's requests to look up shoppers' saved cards, and each time that happened the shop's account page failed along with the lookup. Argus handed the incident to a person. Argus did not test the first candidate it formed (C1): the failure is in a service another company runs, and nothing Argus can do reaches it. Account pages could keep failing for as long as io-pay keeps refusing card lookups, and any later io-pay outage could fail them the same way.

Impact
at least 7m 21s - since onset, still not back to normal
100.0% - peak error rate
9,402 - requests failed
1.1% to 97.9% - what the alert watches, before onset and while broken on average (the rule's line is 10%)
at least 15,583.55 USD - customer loss (estimated)

Root cause and contributing factors
The third-party payment provider io-pay began returning 503 to io-shop's card lookups for shoppers. io-shop's payment provider client (payment_provider.py) raised each of those responses as PaymentProviderFailed, and the account page request failed with it instead of rendering.
Causal chain
symptom Shoppers' account pages failed. Account page requests errored from the onset onward.
  Evidence:
    T5 17:24:11 Investigator Agent: Placed the start of the incident at 17:17
    Gbac1 WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - 5 occurrences in 6 minutes, 17:15–17:20; # was 1.00% to 100.00%, typically 100.00%, highest at 17:18
    Gbf7d ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - PaymentProviderFailed: api.io-pay.example returned 503 for /v1/shoppers/shopper-#-#-#/card at src/io_shop/payment_provider.py:95 - 8 occurrences in 4 minutes, 17:17–17:20; /v1/shoppers/shopper-#-#-#/card took 8 different values
why 1 The failed account page requests were failed card lookups. io-shop's payment provider client raised PaymentProviderFailed when its call for a shopper's card failed, and the page request failed with it.
  Evidence:
    Gbf7d
why 2 The card lookups failed because io-pay, the third-party payment provider that IO Payments Ltd runs, began returning 503 for them at the onset. The record does not show why io-pay failed.
  Evidence:
    Gbf7d
    T9 17:24:13 Investigator Agent: Read the service register - the service calls io-pricing (internal, owned by checkout-platform), io-summary-cache (internal, owned by checkout-platform), io-pay (third-party, owned by IO Payments Ltd)
    T5
  Ruled out:
    A deploy, release or flag change on the service: the Investigator Agent asked for production change events - deploys and releases, and flag changes from the flag provider's history, the 1 day 1 minute before Nov 12 17:18; the Investigator Agent read back 0 production changes. A flag change by anyone but Argus: Argus read the flag provider's history - 0 flag changes by anyone but Argus, the 1 hour before 17:24:15.
      T7
      T8
      T14
    Shoppers closing the connection (ClientDisconnected). Those errors came before the onset, and the next minute's log line shows account pages rendering normally.
      G46bc ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ClientDisconnected: the shopper closed the connection - 2 occurrences in 1 minute, 17:15
      Gad41 INFO io-shop: account pages rendered normally - 1 occurrence in 1 minute, 17:16
Contributing factors
- No fallback was seen for when io-pay's card lookup fails. The account page request failed outright rather than rendering without the card details. (AI-2)
- The HighErrorRate alert on io-shop paged nobody: no on-call incident was linked to it. (AI-3)

Hypotheses considered
 | Hypothesis | Confidence | Result
C1 | From 17:17 UTC the third-party payment provider io-pay (IO Payments Ltd) returned 503 for card lookups. Every account page render needs that call, so io-shop's error rate went to 100% and latency rose to about 2s. io-shop had no deployment or other change in the preceding 24 hours. | 0.93 | never tried: the failure is in a service another company runs, and nothing Argus can do reaches it

Trigger
No trigger was established.

Resolution
 | Time (UTC) | Action | By | Kind | Outcome
 | 17:24:21 | Refused to act on C1 - the failure is in a service another company runs, and nothing Argus can do reaches it - ask IO Payments Ltd to restore io-pay, and no code fix is looked for | Argus | nothing to put back | not taken

Detection
The incident on io-shop began at 17:17 UTC. HighErrorRate fired at 17:23:13 UTC, 6 minutes 13 seconds later.
What the alert said
AL1 | Error rate above threshold for 5m

Action items
Item | Action | Type | Owner | Tracking | Status
AI-1 | Ask IO Payments Ltd to restore io-pay (api.io-pay.example) and to say why it failed | mitigate | unassigned | - | open
AI-2 | Make io-shop's account page render without the card details, instead of failing the whole request, when io-pay's card lookup returns an error. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-3 | Route the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to the on-call rotation so that it pages a person when it fires. | process | unassigned | - | open

Lessons learned
What went well
- The alert came within the 7 minutes 30 seconds accounted for by its rule waiting 5 minutes with its condition holding, its evaluation at intervals of 1 minute, an unmeasured allowance of 30 seconds for scraping and storing its samples and the whole minute the onset is measured to.
- 58 seconds after the alert was raised, the Investigator Agent placed the start of the incident at 17:17.
- 1 minute 2 seconds after the alert was raised, the Investigator Agent formed 1 candidate cause, best first: C1.
- 1 minute 2 seconds after the alert was raised, Argus read the flag provider's history - 0 flag changes by anyone but Argus, the 1 hour before 17:24:15.
- 1 minute 8 seconds after the alert was raised, Argus refused to act on C1 - the failure is in a service another company runs, and nothing Argus can do reaches it - ask IO Payments Ltd to restore io-pay, and no code fix is looked for.
What went wrong
Nothing.
Where it got lucky
Nothing.

Timeline (UTC)

T8 | 17:24:13 |  | Investigator Agent Read back 0 production changes
T9 | 17:24:13 |  | Investigator Agent Read the service register - the service calls io-pricing (internal, owned by checkout-platform), io-summary-cache (internal, owned by checkout-platform), io-pay (third-party, owned by IO Payments Ltd)
T10 | 17:24:13 |  | Investigator Agent Asked for the service's log lines, the 5 minutes before 17:20

T17 | 17:24:21 |  | Argus Moved the incident to FIXING - no mitigation taken

Response effort
none - engineer time
97,478 - tokens spent by Argus

Supporting information
The incident's walk: http://localhost:8000/incidents/42d7f688-1fa4-491f-b41b-ca97167d8f48
Changes to production read
Deploys read, none came back; flags read, none came back.
Log messages read (UTC)
G46bc | ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ClientDisconnected: the shopper closed the connection - 2 occurrences in 1 minute, 17:15
Gbac1 | WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - 5 occurrences in 6 minutes, 17:15–17:20; # was 1.00% to 100.00%, typically 100.00%, highest at 17:18
Gad41 | INFO io-shop: account pages rendered normally - 1 occurrence in 1 minute, 17:16
Gbf7d | ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - PaymentProviderFailed: api.io-pay.example returned 503 for /v1/shoppers/shopper-#-#-#/card at src/io_shop/payment_provider.py:95 - 8 occurrences in 4 minutes, 17:17–17:20; /v1/shoppers/shopper-#-#-#/card took 8 different values
Assumptions
- Exchange rate: EUR converted at 0.92191 per USD, published 2026-11-12
- No engineer minutes: no on-call incident was linked to this one, so nobody was paged to respond

Review checklist
✓ Key incident data collected (met)
○ Impact assessed (for a person)
  the loss is measured to the close; when the service is back to normal is for a person to report
○ Root-cause analysis complete (for a person)
  the failure is in a service another company runs, and nothing Argus can do reaches it
○ Every action item owned and dated (for a person)
○ Reviewed and shared (for a person)

The document, by field:
overview: For {duration}, shoppers on io-shop had their account pages fail. IO Payments Ltd, the outside company that handles the shop's payments, began refusing the shop's requests to look up shoppers' saved cards. Each time a lookup was refused, the shopper's account page failed with it. At the worst minute, {peak_error_rate} of requests were failing. Argus estimates the shop lost {customer_loss} in takings. Nobody was paged, so no on-call responders were called in. Argus did not act on the suspected cause because the failure is in io-pay, a service IO Payments Ltd runs that Argus has no way to reach. Its recommended step is to ask IO Payments Ltd to restore io-pay, and it did not look for a code fix. That step has not been taken.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {duration}, are figures code writes in from the list of figures in the ask. They are not judged.
  - The overview is written in plain words for the people who lead the company. A claim said more plainly than the postmortem says it is grounded where it means the same.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.
